I'll solve this directly. The Fourier cosine transform is defined as

$$\hat f_c(\omega) = \int_0^\infty f(x)\cos(\omega x)\,dx.$$

---

## (a) $f(x)=\sin x$ on $[0,\pi)$, $0$ for $x>\pi$

$$\hat f_c(\omega)=\int_0^\pi \sin x\,\cos(\omega x)\,dx.$$

Using $\sin x\cos(\omega x)=\tfrac12[\sin((1+\omega)x)+\sin((1-\omega)x)]$,

$$\hat f_c(\omega)=\frac12\Big[\frac{-\cos((1+\omega)x)}{1+\omega}+\frac{-\cos((1-\omega)x)}{1-\omega}\Big]_0^\pi.$$

Since $\cos((1+\omega)\pi)=\cos((1-\omega)\pi)=-\cos(\omega\pi)$,

$$\hat f_c(\omega)=\frac12\Big[\frac{1+\cos\omega\pi}{1+\omega}+\frac{1+\cos\omega\pi}{1-\omega}\Big]=\frac{1+\cos\omega\pi}{1-\omega^2}=\frac{2\cos^2(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}.$$

At $\omega=1$ (removable): $\int_0^\pi\sin x\cos x\,dx=\tfrac12\int_0^\pi\sin 2x\,dx=0$, consistent with the limit.

$$\boxed{\hat f_c(\omega)=\frac{1+\cos\omega\pi}{1-\omega^2}=\frac{2\cos^2(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}.}$$

---

## (b) $\phi(x)=h$ on $[0,1/h)$, $0$ for $x>1/h$

$$\hat\phi_c(\omega)=\int_0^{1/h}h\cos(\omega x)\,dx=\frac{h}{\omega}\sin(\omega x)\Big|_0^{1/h}=\frac{h}{\omega}\sin\!\Big(\frac{\omega}{h}\Big).$$

$$\boxed{\hat\phi_c(\omega)=\frac{h}{\omega}\sin\!\Big(\frac{\omega}{h}\Big).}$$

---

## (c) $F(t)=|\cos\pi t|$ on $[0,1)$, $0$ for $t>1$

Since $\cos\pi t\ge 0$ on $[0,\tfrac12]$ and $\le 0$ on $[\tfrac12,1]$,

$$\hat F_c(\omega)=\int_0^{1/2}\cos\pi t\,\cos\omega t\,dt-\int_{1/2}^{1}\cos\pi t\,\cos\omega t\,dt.$$

Let $I(a,b)=\int_a^b\cos\pi t\cos\omega t\,dt=\tfrac12\big[\frac{\sin((\pi-\omega)t)}{\pi-\omega}+\frac{\sin((\pi+\omega)t)}{\pi+\omega}\big]_a^b$.

Using $\sin\big(\tfrac{\pi\mp\omega}{2}\big)=\cos\tfrac{\omega}{2}$, $\sin(\pi\mp\omega)=\pm\sin\omega$:

$$I(0,\tfrac12)=\tfrac12\cos\tfrac{\omega}{2}\Big[\frac1{\pi-\omega}+\frac1{\pi+\omega}\Big]=\frac{\pi\cos(\omega/2)}{\pi^2-\omega^2}.$$

$$I(\tfrac12,1)=\tfrac12\sin\omega\Big[\frac1{\pi-\omega}-\frac1{\pi+\omega}\Big]-\frac{\pi\cos(\omega/2)}{\pi^2-\omega^2}=\frac{\omega\sin\omega-\pi\cos(\omega/2)}{\pi^2-\omega^2}.$$

Therefore

$$\hat F_c(\omega)=I(0,\tfrac12)-I(\tfrac12,1)=\frac{2\pi\cos(\omega/2)-\omega\sin\omega}{\pi^2-\omega^2}.$$

Check $\omega=0$: $\hat F_c(0)=\int_0^1|\cos\pi t|\,dt=\frac2\pi$; formula gives $\frac{2\pi}{\pi^2}=\frac2\pi$. ✓

$$\boxed{\hat F_c(\omega)=\frac{2\pi\cos(\omega/2)-\omega\sin\omega}{\pi^2-\omega^2}.}$$

---

## (d) $G(x)=\cos x$ on $(\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{2})$, $0$ otherwise on $[0,\infty)$

$$\hat G_c(\omega)=\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\cos x\,\cos\omega x\,dx=\frac12\Big[\frac{\sin((1-\omega)x)}{1-\omega}+\frac{\sin((1+\omega)x)}{1+\omega}\Big]_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}.$$

At $x=\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$: $\sin\big(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}(1\mp\omega)\big)=-\cos\big(\tfrac{3\omega\pi}{2}\big)$.
At $x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$: $\sin\big(\tfrac{\pi}{2}(1\mp\omega)\big)=\cos\big(\tfrac{\omega\pi}{2}\big)$.

$$\hat G_c(\omega)=-\frac12\Big[\cos\frac{3\omega\pi}{2}+\cos\frac{\omega\pi}{2}\Big]\Big[\frac1{1-\omega}+\frac1{1+\omega}\Big]=-\frac{\cos(3\omega\pi/2)+\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}.$$

Using $\cos\frac{3\omega\pi}{2}+\cos\frac{\omega\pi}{2}=2\cos(\omega\pi)\cos\frac{\omega\pi}{2}$,

$$\hat G_c(\omega)=-\frac{2\cos(\omega\pi)\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}.$$

Check $\omega=0$: $\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\cos x\,dx=\sin x\big|_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}=-2$; formula gives $-\frac{2}{1}=-2$. ✓
Check $\omega=1$: $\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\cos^2 x\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2}$; L'Hôpital on the $0/0$ form gives $\frac{(3\pi/2)\sin(3\pi/2)+(\pi/2)\sin(\pi/2)}{-2}=\frac{-3\pi/2+\pi/2}{-2}=\frac{\pi}{2}$. ✓

$$\boxed{\hat G_c(\omega)=-\frac{\cos(3\omega\pi/2)+\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}=-\frac{2\cos(\omega\pi)\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}.}$$

---

**Summary of Fourier cosine transforms:**

| Part | Transform |
|---|---|
| (a) | $\dfrac{1+\cos\omega\pi}{1-\omega^2}=\dfrac{2\cos^2(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}$ |
| (b) | $\dfrac{h}{\omega}\sin\!\dfrac{\omega}{h}$ |
| (c) | $\dfrac{2\pi\cos(\omega/2)-\omega\sin\omega}{\pi^2-\omega^2}$ |
| (d) | $-\dfrac{\cos(3\omega\pi/2)+\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}=-\dfrac{2\cos\omega\pi\cos(\omega\pi/2)}{1-\omega^2}$ |
